title: If you can see a toilet from your kitchen island, that's a fail
guestRole: Founder & Principal Architect, DDA Architecture Ltd.
description: Jordan Salvador talks with Marvin DeJong, founder and principal architect at DDA Architecture Ltd., about the residential-design decisions that protect privacy, support long-term durability, and keep a project aligned with the people who will live in it. Marvin explains why spatial planning should separate public and private moments, how material choices affect a home's useful life, and why weekly client conversations prevent late-stage surprises and rework.
takeaways: Privacy starts with spatial planning, including keeping bathrooms and other private moments out of direct view from a home's central living spaces.
Long-lived homes require design and material decisions that prioritize resilience and repairability rather than short-term convenience.
Frequent client conversations keep design intent aligned, expose concerns earlier, and reduce the risk of costly rework after a team has moved too far ahead.

title: Last Year's Plastic Would Build a Bridge to the Moon
description: Jordan Salvador talks with Dustin Bowers, founder and CEO of PLAEX Building Systems, about turning recycled polymers and aggregates into interlocking construction blocks designed for strength, disassembly, and reuse. Dustin explains the commercial case for circular materials, the limitations of linear building methods, and how containerized production lines can help local operators turn regional plastic waste into building products.
takeaways: Interlocking material systems can reduce dependence on mortar while creating a more adaptable approach to wall construction and rain-screen performance.
Designing for disassembly keeps materials in use through renovation, reconfiguration, or reuse instead of treating demolition as the default end state.
Compact production systems can support a licensing model that converts local plastic-waste streams into regional construction materials.

title: You Designed Your Home Around a Storage Unit
description: Jordan Salvador talks with Dan Romanko, registered professional planner, chartered new urbanist, and principal of Better Neighbourhoods Inc., about the land-development decisions that shape daily life. Dan explains the hidden cost of front-loaded garages, why laneway garages can improve both lot value and walkability, how local approvals really work, and where LIDAR, AI rendering, and contextual models can help planners communicate a proposal without replacing professional judgment.
takeaways: Street and garage design affect light, walkability, and the long-term value people experience in a neighbourhood.
Putting garages on laneways can create a more usable streetscape while giving developers a stronger land-value proposition.
LIDAR-derived context models and AI visualization can clarify a land-development conversation when the underlying site information is accurate.

title: Every Architect Told Him Not to Do It. He Did It Anyway
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Paul Hirst, principal of Hirst Design in Utah, to discuss an architecture practice shaped by structural-engineering training, custom residential work, and a willingness to challenge familiar assumptions. Paul shares his views on building-performance trade-offs, sustainability marketing, patterns of living, and the boundary he draws between AI-assisted efficiency and the human responsibility to design.
takeaways: Building-performance decisions are strongest when teams weigh the whole envelope, client priorities, and long-term trade-offs instead of optimizing for a label alone.
The questions asked before the first line is drawn help an architect create a home around the way a client actually lives.
AI can reduce research and production friction, but design judgment remains a professional responsibility that should stay with people.

title: He Inherited a Business and a 1997 Email Client
description: Jordan Salvador talks with Derrick Lawless, owner of D. Lawless Hardware, about rebuilding a national hardware distribution and e-commerce business after inheriting both a family legacy and a 1997 email client. Derrick explains how he removed single-person bottlenecks, rebuilt legacy operations, protected specialist product lines, and is using AI discovery and verification loops to make the business easier to find and operate.
takeaways: Modernizing a business starts by making critical knowledge and workflows accessible to more than one person.
Leaner operations are strongest when repetitive work is redesigned thoughtfully, not when people are treated as costs to remove.
AI discovery can surface specialist products and expertise when the underlying information is structured, specific, and verified by people.

title: What Actually Fixes the Housing Crisis
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Michelle Sablack, partner at Chicago-based WJW Architects, to examine what genuinely moves the needle on affordable housing. Michelle shares WJW's evidence-informed design approach, the economics of sustainability for residents, honest AIA 2030 reporting, and the human questions surrounding AI adoption inside a design practice.
takeaways: Evidence-informed design and post-occupancy learning keep resident outcomes at the center of affordable-housing decisions.
For residents who pay the utility bills, sustainability is an affordability and resilience strategy, not just a design value.
AI adoption works best when leaders listen to staff concerns before deciding how new tools belong in the practice.

title: His Colleagues Say He's Killing the Profession. He Says He's Saving It.
description: Jordan Salvador talks with Richard Taylor, founder of Sketch House, about making residential architecture more accessible through transparent fixed pricing and high-volume systems. Richard explains how his eight-person team starts four to six projects each week, uses point-cloud scanning and AI-assisted design tools, and gives clients immersive ways to experience a project before construction.
takeaways: Transparent fixed pricing can make architectural services easier for homeowners to understand, buy, and plan for.
Point-cloud scanning and repeatable operating systems let a small team handle more projects without treating design as a commodity.
AI and immersive visualization help clients communicate design intent earlier, reducing ambiguity before construction begins.

title: Flying Blind in Clean Energy: The Biogas Intelligence Gap
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Kim Kupiecki, founder of Alchemyca Biotech, to unpack the data gap affecting biogas and renewable natural gas operators. Kim explains how the Claritix platform brings reliable operating intelligence to a complex sector, what unreliable data costs the industry, and where AI can accelerate the next phase of the clean-energy transition.
takeaways: Biogas and renewable-natural-gas operators cannot optimize performance when critical operating data is fragmented or unreliable.
A shared intelligence layer turns complex plant information into faster, more confident operating decisions.
AI creates the most value in clean energy when it is built on trustworthy data rather than added on top of blind spots.

title: No Clients, No Safety Net, Just Conviction
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Jorge Herrera, founder of the luxury residential architecture firm Halo, to explore his career journey and design philosophy. Jorge shares how he made the leap to start his own firm with no clients and no safety net, driven purely by conviction, and how he now integrates AI into architectural rendering and client presentations to deliver a higher standard of design.

title: The AI That Never Lets You Lose on Your Energy Bill
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with James Grasso, founder of Kilowatt, to discuss the history of energy deregulation and the challenges consumers face in navigating the complex retail energy market. James highlights the prevalence of misleading marketing tactics and introduces Kilowatt as an AI-powered solution designed to automate energy procurement and secure the best rates for consumers.

title: Why 70 Units on 580 Acres Beat Every Developer's 700
guestRole: Founding Principal & CEO, Pfeffer Torode Architecture
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Jamie Pfeffer, founding principal and CEO of Pfeffer Torode Architecture and Interior Design Studio, to discuss design as a powerful business strategy. Jamie shares how his conviction-driven approach to design, building 70 units on 580 acres, outperformed conventional developer logic and delivered exceptional returns.

title: The Architect Who Wins by Knowing What Nobody Else Bothers to Learn
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Dovid Feld, principal of Feld & Associates in Los Angeles, to discuss how he built a niche-dominant architecture firm by focusing on education rather than traditional marketing. Dovid explains how leveraging deep code knowledge as a business model has made his firm the go-to resource in its market.

title: The Emergency Landing That Built an AI Architecture Firm
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Jair Ibarra, co-founder of Rootherhub, who recounts how a stressful emergency landing experience ultimately inspired him to establish an AI architecture firm. The conversation explores how this pivotal moment shaped the vision and foundation of his AI-driven design and consulting company.

title: A 2-Person Architecture Firm Winning 200-Person Projects
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Mariusz Klemens, co-founder and principal of Open Architecture Office (OAO), to discuss how an AI-first operating system allows a two-person team to efficiently compete for and win large-scale projects. They explore how integrating AI into the firm's foundation has fundamentally changed traditional architectural workflows and business models.

title: America Is 20 Years Behind on Modular Building
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with David Den Daas, founder of Urban Lab Architecture in Washington, DC, to discuss why America is 20 years behind on modular building. David explains that America is still building with wood modules that require wide-load trucks and special permits, a method the rest of the world figured out decades ago.

title: True Luxury Is Feeling Healthy in Your Home
guestRole: Distinguished Fellow, AIBD: 40 Years of Wellness Design
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Jenny Pippin, Distinguished Fellow of the AIBD with 40 years of wellness design experience, to discuss how true luxury is feeling healthy in your home. They delve into wellness design, hidden accessibility features, and what most homes are missing for optimal health and resale value.

title: By the Time You Protest, It's Already Built
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Isaiah Ness, CEO of Sun Bear Industries, to discuss the critical need for energy infrastructure and economic sovereignty in underserved communities, particularly tribal nations. They explore the fragility of the current energy grid, the impact of rising power demands from data centers, and how Sun Bear Industries is empowering communities to build and own their own renewable energy assets.

title: The AEC Industry Has Been Hallucinating for Decades
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Kimon Onuma to discuss how the AEC industry has been making things up, missing specs, and burying intelligence in PDFs for decades. Kimon argues that when someone says AI hallucinates, it's a familiar concept to anyone who has worked in AEC, and explains how the industry can finally fix it.

title: He Built Paul Allen's $250M Yacht. Now He's Building AI Systems.
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Mark Buchanan, who famously built Paul Allen's $250 million yacht, to discuss his remarkable transition into building AI systems. Mark shares his framework for efficient contextual AI and how lessons from high-stakes yacht construction translate directly into scalable AI architecture.

title: It's Only Pretty Pictures Until It's Built
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Brian Baber to discuss the realities of building and construction beyond initial designs. They delve into the challenges of allowances in interior design and the critical strategy of specifying every item before a build contract is signed. Pretty pictures mean nothing until they're built.

title: The Hire That Changed Everything
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Dan Mayer, founder of Development Architecture Collaborative, to discuss how a single strategic hire, despite having no prior architecture experience, led to a remarkable 69% revenue growth for his firm in one year. Dan shares the insights behind this pivotal decision and its transformative impact.

title: The Housing Crisis Is a Process Problem
description: Jordan Salvador discusses the housing crisis and reframes it as a process problem rather than a supply problem. The episode delves into why treating apartments like custom homes, misalignment between developers, designers, and builders, and broken coordination workflows are the real culprits behind unaffordable housing.

title: Architecture Is Broken and AI Is About to Expose It
description: Jordan Salvador discusses how the field of architecture is facing significant systemic challenges, and how artificial intelligence is poised to expose and potentially address them. The episode explores the current state of architectural practice and the transformative impact AI could have on the industry's most entrenched problems.

title: The Food System Is Fragile. Rob Built a Property That Isn't.
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Rob Avis, co-founder of 5th World, to discuss the urgent need for regenerative development and autonomous living systems. They explore the fragility of modern centralized food and energy systems, advocating for homes that produce their own resources. Avis shares insights from his journey from the industrial food sector to founding 5th World, emphasizing design that harmonizes with ecological patterns.

title: Rebuilding the Bronx One Project at a Time
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Aishah Coleman, who runs a 16-year architecture and design firm, to discuss her journey of rebuilding the Bronx one project at a time. Coleman shares her experience completing a $72 million project ahead of schedule and under budget, and the challenges she faced in the aftermath.

title: Architecture Isn't Enough Anymore (Here's What Actually Wins Projects)
description: Jordan Salvador discusses why traditional architecture alone is no longer sufficient for winning projects in today's competitive landscape. He explores the critical factors, from authority positioning to AI-driven outreach, that actually move the needle for AEC firms looking to grow.

title: Rethinking Workforce Lodging in Construction
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Richard Grier, co-founder of Hard Hat Housing, to discuss the critical need for better workforce lodging in the construction industry. They explore how Hard Hat Housing is moving away from traditional hotel stays to provide home-like accommodations, ultimately improving the mental health and retention of traveling crews.

title: Why High-Performance Homes Fail at Construction
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Mike Mahon, CEO of Adaptive Building, to discuss the realities of building high-performance, net-zero homes and why innovation in this space often fails at the construction phase. They explore how Adaptive Building navigates these challenges by focusing on system readiness, team alignment, and client education.

title: Why Most Construction Companies Are Not Ready for AI
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Mike Kanaby of Profitability Works to discuss why many construction companies are not prepared to implement AI. They explore the necessity of establishing standardized processes and centralized data before adopting new technologies. Without a strong operational foundation, AI will only amplify existing chaos.

title: AI for Manufacturing Growth: From Real-Time Data to Scalable Factory Performance
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Zakary Smith of Sensflo to discuss how leading manufacturers are using AI to scale operations, reduce downtime, and improve efficiency. They delve into how real-time factory data and machine monitoring are driving the next generation of scalable industrial performance.

title: $1 Billion AI Buildings Are Coming… But There's One Big Problem
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Tiemo Mehner of DCM Designs to discuss how the AI boom is reshaping data center design, architecture, and infrastructure planning. They explore the challenges and opportunities of $1 billion AI buildings and the future of hyperscale data center construction.

title: How He Scaled a Design Build Firm to 300 Projects Per Year
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Edgar Vidal, founder of Dreams Design Build in Los Angeles, to discuss how he built a high-volume architecture, construction, and real estate development business. Edgar shares how he uses systems, leadership, and smarter upfront planning to scale his firm to 300 projects per year without chaos.

title: Innovation and AI in the Built Environment
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Brent Eubanks, founder of Eubanks Engineering Research, to discuss practical approaches to innovation within the engineering and built environment sectors. The conversation covers Eubanks' multidisciplinary career, the difference between true innovation and mere disruption, and the future of predictive building controls.

title: From Chaos to Clarity: How AI Is Reinventing Operations
description: Jordan Salvador discusses how AI is reinventing operations in the construction industry, addressing coordination bottlenecks and optimizing workflows. The episode covers the next generation of construction technology and how firms can move from operational chaos to clarity using intelligent automation.

title: Can Old Tires Fix America's Pothole Problem?
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Xan Dif to discuss a civil engineering solution to America's pothole problem. The episode explores why roads fail and how recycled tire rubber could be used to build and maintain more durable, cost-effective road infrastructure across the country.

title: The System That Could Change How Homes Are Built
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Katie Reynolds and Mike Gwynn of Shibusa Systems to discuss their innovative work transforming the home building industry. They explore how Shibusa is delivering climate-resilient, elegant housing that is faster, more sustainable, and more economical than traditional construction methods.

title: Can You Build a Successful Business Without Sacrificing Your Family?
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Brian Baber to discuss the real tension between building a successful business and maintaining a thriving family life. They explore practical frameworks for entrepreneurs in the AEC space who want to scale without sacrificing the relationships that matter most.

title: Concrete Isn't Always the Best Option: How RMP Is Winning Infrastructure Projects Anyway
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Doug Talbott of RMP Global to break down how infrastructure projects are really won, long before the RFP is issued. Doug explains that you don't need to be specified to win the job, and shares how RMP is winning major infrastructure contracts by challenging the assumption that concrete is always the best option.

title: Most Energy-Efficient Homes Miss the One Thing That Actually Matters
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Rahul Shah, founder of Tight House, to explore what if the most sustainable homes aren't the ones with the best metrics, but the ones that feel right to live in. They discuss how energy efficiency without livability is an incomplete solution, and what truly matters in high-performance home design.

title: Why Sports Facilities Are Bleeding Energy Costs (And How Smart Owners Fix It)
description: Jordan Salvador discusses how sports facility owners are facing mounting pressure to reduce operating costs and improve comfort, while many are still using outdated energy and automation systems. He breaks down the smart building strategies that forward-thinking owners are using to cut energy costs and future-proof their facilities.

title: This Patented Energy System Could Decentralize Power Forever
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Charles Wilson, Founder and CEO of TransElectric Corp, to discuss a patented energy system that could decentralize power generation forever. They explore what it would mean for every home to generate its own clean power and feed energy back into the grid.

title: Design Leadership Isn't About Aesthetics: It's About Sustainability & Accountability
guestRole: Principal Architect, RS Mannino Architects and Builders
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Rosario Mannino, Principal Architect at RS Mannino Architects and Builders, to discuss his transition from traditional architecture roles to founding his own design-build firm. They explore design leadership as accountability and vision, the use of durable natural materials, and the future impact of AI on architectural practice.

title: ESG Certifications Exposed: How to Streamline Compliance, Win Investors & Scale Faster
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Dr. Rachana Malviya, founder of Greenloop Clean Tech, to discuss the challenges of project certification and how strategic innovation and technology can streamline compliance. They explore the growing importance of ESG reporting, carbon accounting, and how businesses can navigate complex global regulatory environments.

title: Beyond the Codes: How to Simplify Regulations & Turn Compliance Into an Advantage
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Jonathan Wolk, founder of Wolk360, to discuss how his company is reshaping how the construction industry navigates codes, compliance, and regulations. Jonathan shares his intuitive approach that helps companies stay compliant while saving time and turning regulatory complexity into a competitive advantage.

title: Why Client Education Is the Secret to Profitable, Sustainable Architecture
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Aaron Olko, Managing Principal at TLRS, to explore how thoughtful client education transforms architecture, planning, and sustainable design. Aaron breaks down how TLRS is rethinking materials, sustainability, and client communication, including compressed earth construction, biophilic design, and the growing role of AI in modern practice.

title: Why Steel Is Replacing Wood in Construction: Intellisteel's Breakthrough Explained
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Stanley Adwell, founder of Intellisteel, to unpack one of the biggest paradigm shifts in modern construction. Stanley shares how Intellisteel's mobile, on-site steel manufacturing technology is outperforming wood and concrete on cost, speed, durability, and certification, solving problems the construction industry has struggled with for over 150 years.

title: Biophilic Architecture Explained: How Mon.Archi Designs Healthier, Human-Centered Spaces
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Carlos A. Monsalve, founder of Mon.Archi, to discuss biophilic design, cultural context, and human-centered architecture. They explore sustainable design philosophy, common misconceptions about cost, and how nature-integrated spaces improve health, well-being, and everyday life.

title: Building the Future With Hempcrete: Scott Black on Non-Toxic Construction & Dome Gaia Solutions
guestRole: Non-Toxic Construction Expert & Dome Gaia Solutions
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Scott Black to discuss building the future with hempcrete and non-toxic construction methods. They spotlight how Dome Gaia Solutions is redefining construction, sustainability, and the future of the built environment through natural, health-conscious building materials.

title: How Verdant Structural Engineering Builds Greener, Smarter Buildings
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Anthony Dente of Verdant Structural Engineering to unpack how structural innovation and sustainability are reshaping the future of green building. They dive into how Verdant balances cost, safety, and performance, and explore how AI, data, and digital tools can help engineers design faster, cut waste, and deliver greener projects.

title: How Architects Scale Without Selling Out
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Elias Horvat, founder of Creates Cool, to discuss his journey in the architecture industry and the founding of his firm. They explore the common dilemma of whether scaling a business requires compromising on core values, with Elias sharing insights on achieving sustainable growth while remaining true to your principles.

title: How to Cut 50% Off Architecture Permitting Time: Digital Construction & AI
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Louai Alsaman, architect and Fulbright scholar at RenderExpo, to discuss how digital construction and 3D visualizations can cut architecture permitting time by 50%. They explore how AI tools reduce waste and miscommunication in the architectural process, dramatically accelerating project delivery.

title: How Essayons Engineers Scales Surveying & Engineering: Boundary Surveys, Land Development & Growth
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Andy Whaley, founder of Essayons Engineers, to explore how engineering and surveying firms can break out of the feast-and-famine cycle and scale using smart systems, consistent client acquisition, and AI-powered workflows.

title: How Emotive Architecture Is Redefining Design in DC
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Aubrey Grant, founder of Emotive Architecture, to discuss how Emotive Architecture is reshaping Washington DC's built environment through empathy-driven, human-centered design. They also discuss the realities of growing an architecture studio, competing in a saturated market, and navigating long AEC sales cycles.

title: The $45M Revolution in Modular Construction: How Hopewell360 Is Building Smarter, Greener Homes
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with TJ Hammerstrom, Founder and CEO of Hopewell360, for a deep dive into how modular, net-zero-ready construction is about to disrupt the $4 trillion U.S. housing market. TJ shares how Hopewell360 is building homes that are faster, smarter, and greener, redefining the future of sustainable development.

title: How Tiny Homes Are Solving the Housing Crisis
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Breno Neri, Co-Founder and President of Contemporary Tiny Homes, to explore how Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) and sustainable design are transforming the housing landscape. They discuss how tiny homes can solve housing affordability and create passive income, focusing on their impact across the Northeast.

title: Solar CEO Reveals Why Renewable Projects Waste Millions
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Collin Rhodes, VP at Somos Solar in New Mexico, to discuss what's really behind project waste in the renewable energy sector. Collin reveals the systemic inefficiencies that cause renewable projects to waste millions and shares what forward-thinking solar companies are doing differently.

title: This Block Could Redefine Housing: Glohab's Daniel Correa on Sustainable Construction
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Daniel Correa of Glohab to discuss a revolutionary building block system that could redefine how homes are constructed. They explore how Glohab's sustainable construction technology is challenging conventional building methods and opening new possibilities for affordable, resilient housing.

title: Smart Cities, Green Tech & the Fight for Water
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Austin Arrington of Plant Group to discuss smart cities, green technology, and the critical issue of water scarcity. The episode explores the intersection of urban development, environmental innovation, and the global fight for sustainable water resources.

title: How Kai Pono Solutions Is Reinventing Stormwater Filtration to Protect Our Oceans
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Navy McKee, CEO and Co-Founder of Kai Pono Solutions, to discuss how Kai Pono is reinventing stormwater filtration to protect our oceans. The episode covers the challenges of breaking into infrastructure, navigating complex stormwater regulations, and scaling manufacturing while keeping ocean health at the heart of their mission.

title: Future-Proofing Design: How OFA Group Blends AI & Sustainability
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Thomas Gaffney, COO of OFA Group, to discuss how OFA Group is leading the charge in transforming design and building with AI and sustainability. Thomas shares his journey from law to tech to architecture, which shaped his mission to disrupt an industry known for slow permitting and costly delays.

title: Not Just Talk: Solving Real Global Problems That Matter
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Clayton from IDEAS For Us, a global environmental non-profit, to discuss how IDEAS For Us transforms local ideas into real-world climate solutions. The conversation goes beyond talk to explore actionable frameworks for solving the global environmental challenges that matter most.

title: Wildfire-Resilient Homes: Passive House + Prefab Tech Driving the Future of Sustainable Building
guest: Tim Sweeney, Tim Lorang & James Croft
guestRole: Simplus Systems: Wildfire-Resilient Passive House Innovators
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Tim Sweeney, Tim Lorang, and James Croft of Simplus Systems to discuss how sustainable building, Passive House certification, and prefabricated technology can protect communities from wildfires, hurricanes, and other disasters. They explore the future of resilient, climate-ready housing.

title: Blue Planet Systems: Turning CO₂ into Net-Zero Concrete
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Brent Constantz, CEO of Blue Planet Systems, to discuss his company's innovative approach to climate tech. They explore how Blue Planet Systems is transforming carbon emissions into building materials, specifically limestone aggregate for concrete, by mimicking natural biomineralization processes.

title: Building the Future: Modular Construction, Smart Cities & Green Innovation
description: Jordan Salvador sits down with Jessica Lewis, CEO of Mobu Enterprises and Shipping Living, to explore the innovative use of shipping containers in modern construction. They discuss how her companies repurpose containers for sustainable residential, commercial, and agricultural applications, including climate-controlled vertical farms, and the push toward eco-friendly, accessible housing solutions.
